title: Brits Now Track Four Health Habits a Day
paragraphs: How many steps did you take today? How many hours of sleep did you get? And did you drink enough water?

For many people in the UK, checking numbers like these is now part of everyday life. A new OnePoll survey of 2,000 adults found that the average Brit tracks four aspects of their health and lifestyle each day.

Steps, exercise and sleep were among the things people track the most. But many are also looking at things like how much water and protein they're getting, their breathing rate and "body battery" — a measure some fitness devices use to show a person's energy levels.
Perhaps unsurprisingly, younger adults are tracking the most. Those aged 45 and under track an average of five things a day, while those aged 62 and over track fewer than three.

And health tracking is only getting more popular. Over the past five years, sleep tracking has more than doubled, increasing by 108%. Counting daily steps has increased by 72%, while water tracking is up 65%.
Weight was the only measure to become less popular, though, with 3% fewer people tracking it.

All those numbers are having an impact — 43% of people said tracking had made them change something about their lifestyle. Among them, 51% started walking more, 49% drank more water and 45% exercised more.
The survey also found that the average person in the UK walks 7,135 steps a day, gets about six and a half hours of sleep and drinks 1.2 liters of water.
And people do like hitting their targets! Seven in ten said meeting their daily targets encourages them to keep up healthier habits.
